requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finds commodities as the trader types, and the real frontend does the same behind a component that still works without JavaScript. Built outside this programme: EUDPA-616 'Add a search type-ahead for choosing commodities, reusable across the journey' owns it, with the germinal catalogue it searches owned by EUDPA-569 'Germinal | Commodity search' (ruling 10 November), so the waiting-on-design row inc-014 is dropped.

requirements.statement: A visually hidden polite live region announces how many species a typed search lists, counting species rather than commodity headings, reading '3 results available' for three and '1 result available' for one, and 'No results found' when none match, and announces nothing while the typed search is shorter than three characters.
requirements.why: Results that change as the trader types must be announced to screen reader users. Built outside this programme: EUDPA-616 owns the commodity type-ahead and EUDPA-569 the germinal catalogue it searches (ruling 10 November), so the waiting-on-design row inc-014 is dropped.

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader tick several species from one search without losing the search or the selection. Built outside this programme: EUDPA-616 owns the commodity type-ahead and EUDPA-569 the germinal catalogue it searches (ruling 10 November), so the waiting-on-design row inc-014 is dropped.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-064 and -p9-065 show the tick, the kept search text and the in-place update with focus returned to the search box; trace-animals-fit-p8-019 captured the earlier server round trip (c-374).

requirements.statement: Search results list commodities alphabetically by commodity name, and the species under each alphabetically by their label ('common name (Latin name)', or 'commodity name (Latin name)' where a species has no common name), ignoring case and accents.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sorts results so a trader can scan them, for example 'cattle' lists African buffalo first and Yak last. How a list reads, its order included, follows the prototype, and a reference list is never a reason to block a row (ruling 11 November), so the order is not held back by the commodity list's content. The reference service returns groups and species in MDM's own order, so the order is the frontend's to set.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the groups run in ascending commodity-code order and the species inside a group in ascending species-label order (repo-frontend-p9-019, -p9-103, repo-tests-p1-117), over results the reference service returns in MDM's order (repo-referencedata-p2-023).

requirements.statement: In the search results the text that matched the query is shown in bold, in both the commodity header and the species labels (for example 'Domestic **cattle** (Bos taurus)'), with the labels escaped as text before the bold is applied.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the trader why each result matched; escaping the label first means a label always shows as text and can never inject markup.

requirements.statement: Search results are grouped under a header naming the commodity and its code ('Cattle (0102)'), falling back to the bare code where no name is held for it; the header cannot be ticked, each species under it is a small GOV.UK checkbox, and a query that matches a commodity's code lists every species of that commodity.

requirements.statement: A search of three or more characters that matches nothing says 'No results found' and lists no checkboxes.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not show a no-match state; the real service's message stays so a trader is not left with a blank page.

requirements.statement: The selected panel lists each chosen commodity, in commodity-code order and each once, as a bold 'Commodity (code):' line followed by one chip per chosen species, the chip reading 'common name (Latin name)' where the species has a common name (for example 'Cattle (0102):' then 'Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)') and the Latin name alone where it has none.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what has been chosen as removable chips that name the species the way the trader found it. Where the prototype shows a chip with the Latin name alone, it is because its demo entry carries no common name, which the real list's own entries decide.

conflicts.about: Who owns the commodity search: Design Release 2.1's browser component, the server-side search the real frontend had, or the separate commodity-search ticket the 10 November ruling hands it to.

positions.says: The search is a browser component with an icon button, a results list and a polite live region.
The whole live-animals catalogue is embedded in the page as JSON and no request is made while searching.
A search is only run once the trader has typed three characters or more, on the server.
With JavaScript on, typing in the search box lists the matching species in place without a Search press.
DR1's live typing was rebuilt as a static server-rendered page, which cannot convey live typing.
The real search runs only on a Search button press, as a server round trip.
inc-014 is kept because the commodity catalogue is too big for the page.
Commodity search as you type waits on design, because today's server-side search with its Search button already works without JavaScript.
The as-you-type design increment is also blocked on commodities coming from MDM.
Commodities search is handled by a different ticket, not by this work.
This ruling does not settle commodity search as you type: it still waits on its own ticket.
Once a species is ticked, the live region reads '1 option selected' and keeps reading that on later searches instead of the result count.

conflicts.outcome: Ruling 10 November, the highest-ranked source, wins: the commodity search is a separate ticket's work rather than this programme's, so nothing here builds or changes the search control. What that ticket has already built stands and is recorded as it is: the as-you-type list, its guarded results address and its results-count announcement (req-072, req-073, req-074), with the server-side search behind its Search button and its three-character minimum still working without JavaScript (req-1918, req-2227). Design Release 2.1's icon-only search button, its selection-count announcements, its 'Commodity search results' label, its Escape-empties-the-field behaviour and its hidden search terms go out of scope as that ticket's to decide (req-2229, req-2230, req-2231, req-2583). Ruling 2026-10-09's reason for keeping inc-014 (claim 117) stays withdrawn, and the 9 October afternoon design wait is replaced by the 10 November handover; ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-059 and -p1-060 are not overruled, because they also record that the server-side search works without JavaScript, which req-1918 keeps. The prototype's whole catalogue shipped with the page is not copied, because the real list is MDM's and far too large for the page. The prototype's live region switching to '1 option selected' once a species is ticked is one of those selection-count announcements and is set aside with them, so the results-count announcement req-073 records stands.

The hint that shipped departed from that wording, and which wording ships is open and unruled.
